A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sharpness-Aware Machine Unlearning work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original unlearning experiments, including accuracy, ToW, membership-inference, sensitivity and representation analyses on image-classification datasets.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds corruption, relearning, architecture, efficiency and KLoM evaluations.

M1.justification: The retain-SAM/forget-sharpness-maximization design remains. However, v1 Appendix C.1 selects parameters with the largest gradient magnitudes, whereas v2 Section 3.2 and Algorithm 1 specify the smallest; v2 Appendix E.2 still says largest. This inconsistency prevents determining whether the masking procedure actually changed.

E1.justification: CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1K, CIFAR-10 and Tiny-ImageNet are retained. Coverage expands through CIFAR-100 scenarios with glass-blur and snow corruption and subsequent forget-set relearning attacks (Appendices G.3 and G.5). These are limited scenario extensions within the existing image-classification domain.

E2.justification: The original comparator sets remain. Table 17 adds Momentum SAM comparisons against SGD and ASAM for L1-Sparse, NegGrad, Sharp MinMax, RL and SalUn, extending the optimizer comparisons without replacing the established baselines.

E3.justification: New evaluation protocols include ViT-Small with AdamW, mask-cutoff sweeps, one-epoch relearning at three learning rates, runtime comparisons and KLoM distributional evaluation with 10 bins. Section 4.3 also drops the denominator factor 1/2 from the variance-entanglement formula, although Table 4 is unchanged; this establishes a reported formula revision, not an experimental rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a 10%/30%/50% masking ablation, structured-noise robustness tests, relearning attacks, architecture/optimizer generality checks, efficiency tradeoffs and KLoM tail analysis (Table 7 and Appendices G.3–G.7). These test substantial additional questions beyond the retained alpha sensitivity and loss-landscape analyses.

E5.justification: Three-seed experiments and mu ± 2 sigma error bars already appear in v1 Appendix E.1 and remain in v2. v2 additionally reports N=10 model-based KLoM estimation and 95th-percentile summaries. Table 8 numerically tabulates existing main-experiment uncertainty; it does not establish an increase in those runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the matching original appendix tables retain their scores. New Tables 7 and 14–18 add substantial masking, corruption, ViT, relearning, runtime/MSAM and KLoM results. For example, the new Table 18 comparison reports average KLoM of 0.0973 for SGD versus 0.0827 for SAM unlearning under SGD pretraining, although its forget-set tail results do not uniformly favor SAM.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.2–3.3 revise their statements using beta-dependent limits and omit explicit convergence-epoch bounds. The limiting calculations already existed in v1 Appendix B, and the proofs are essentially retained. The raw variance-entanglement definition also changes through removal of its denominator factor 1/2.

C1.justification: The central claims about SAM's forget-set denoising failure, retain-signal surplus and Sharp MinMax remain. The abstract extends the claimed applicability to corrupted data, different optimizers and different architectures.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 adds the substantive limitation that ascent-induced misclassification can disagree with retraining and permit leakage. New discussions interpret corruption robustness, relearning resistance, overparameterization-dependent masking and MSAM tradeoffs. The feature interpretation also shifts toward SAM preserving retain clusters while SGD scatters retained features.

D1.justification: v2 adds explicit WeightMask and SharpMinMax pseudocode, ViT/AdamW hyperparameters, relearning learning rates, KLoM estimation details and runtime reporting. These substantially expand implementation documentation, although the masking-direction contradiction limits reproducibility. Hardware information and the promise of a future code release remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting Momentum SAM, KLoM/data dependencies, ViTs, AdamW, corruptions and ascent-based unlearning limitations. It also positions efficient SAM variants as an additional contribution. The original related-work survey and broad research positioning are largely retained.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain. v2 simplifies main-text notation, revises method explanations and empirical discussion, and reorganizes the appendices around statements, a notation glossary and a dedicated implementation subsection.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the UMAP figures, expands the main feature illustration to include Sharp MinMax, and switches the main feature and landscape examples to medium memorization. It redesigns and relocates uncertainty plots, adds notation and experimental tables plus algorithm listings, and adopts the ICLR layout. The complete landscape results are retained.

improvement.justification: The added KLoM, corruption, relearning and masking checks strengthen evaluation beyond v1, while qualified theorem statements and the ascent-objective limitation improve precision. The net gain is limited by contradictory masking instructions and claims of uniform robustness and tail improvement that Tables 16 and 18 do not fully support.
